title: Austrian Ball 2019 in London - How to dance Quadrille 1

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher provides clear, concise verbal instructions while standing to the side of the dancers. She uses a formal, structured approach to explain each sequence of the Quadrille.

lesson_structure.note: The teacher introduces the first part of the Quadrille.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the changing of places.
The teacher explains the side steps and the curtsy/nod.
The teacher explains the touch and circle step.
The teacher explains the ladies' solo.
The teacher explains the final part, which repeats the beginning.
The dancers perform the full sequence with music.

cues: take all four steps to the side
touch right hand to right hand

steps_taught.name: changing of places
steps_taught.description: Dancers swap positions with their partners.

steps_taught.name: side steps
steps_taught.description: Dancers take four steps to the side.

steps_taught.name: curtsy/nod
steps_taught.description: Ladies curtsy and gentlemen nod to the outside.

steps_taught.name: touch and circle
steps_taught.description: Dancers touch right hands and walk in a circle.

steps_taught.name: ladies' solo
steps_taught.description: Ladies meet and greet in a figure of eight to change partners.

what_works: The teacher breaks the dance into distinct, manageable segments.
The verbal cues are synchronized with the counts.
what_hinders: The camera angle is static and does not show footwork clearly.

quotes.text: Quadrille number one begins with an intro of eight bars.
The next part is, we take all four steps to the side.
The next part is that we touch, right hand to right hand.
The last part is like the beginning.

evidence_segments.observation: The dancers move in a line, swapping positions with their partners.
The dancers step to the side and perform a curtsy or nod.
The dancers touch right hands and walk in a circle.
The ladies move in a figure-of-eight pattern to change partners.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher uses a 'call and response' style where she speaks the instructions while the dancers perform the movements simultaneously.
